description: Turn approval waits into mobile-first inline review packages with guided send-back feedback and safe, discoverable issue-detail keyboard actions.

tasks.title: Deliver the inline approval review package
tasks.description: Implement the complete approval-specific issue decision surface for Plan and Check, including current-run inline evidence, responsive action access, and independent unavailable states. Replace duplicated desktop/mobile send-back drafts with one controlled direction/scope/detail form that serializes to the existing text feedback contract, while leaving every non-approval state unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: IssueDetailPage detects approval mode only from the derived approval-required decision and mounts one page-local ApprovalReviewPackage at the existing top decision position; non-approval desktop and mobile decision presentations retain their existing behavior and authorized action set.

The Plan package queries exact current-run paths and renders proposal.md through MarkdownReader plus raw recorded tasks.json in a wrapped pre without requiring file selection or a dialog; list loading/error, missing, content loading/error, and unexpected-directory states are identified independently for each artifact.

The Check package renders review.md inline plus a compact current diff summary containing compared branches, files changed, additions, and deletions; transport failure and available:false are distinct inline states and neither suppresses an available review.md.

Artifact-list cache identity includes workflowRunId without changing the HTTP request, exact-path selection does not depend on displayName, suffix matching, or API array order, and a focused query test proves a run-ID change cannot reuse the prior run's list result.

Artifact text rendering is shared with the existing dialog: Markdown behavior remains unchanged, JSON and other text remain raw, and min-width, pre-wrap, word-break, and overflow-wrap constraints prevent long unbroken values from widening the issue page.

Desktop composes the existing IssueDecisionSurface and controller with inline evidence; phone width renders the same evidence plus an approval-specific fixed safe-area-aware bar with direct Approve and Send back controls, stable action tracks, reserved page padding, and no generic action-sheet launcher, action drawer, or dialog in the approval path.

The phone package partitions the existing ordered descriptor list without deriving a second action model: Approve and Send back render directly, every remaining applicable descriptor renders exactly once in an optional compact non-modal More actions menu, and the menu is absent when no secondary descriptor exists; secondary navigation, controller dispatch, pending state, disabled reasons, and ordering match desktop.

During approval, the lower LatestArtifactsPanel and standalone diff-summary banner do not duplicate package evidence; workflow history, sessions, task progress, changed-files navigation, comments, Ask Agent, concrete transcript navigation, and the sole controller-backed action paths remain available.

One controlled SendBackFeedbackForm is used by desktop and mobile with a required single category choice of direction, scope, or detail and required nonblank free text; on a phone, one tap on direct Send back reveals and focuses the form inline without modal semantics, and cancellation, viewport changes, pending state, validation, and errors cannot create divergent drafts or duplicate dispatch.

One tap on the direct phone Approve control dispatches the existing authorized approve descriptor exactly once without an intervening disclosure; one tap on direct Send back opens the inline form, and its successful submission uses the same controller and serialized feedback body as desktop.

Submitting send-back produces exactly one body in the stable form Category: <Title-cased category>, a blank line, and the trimmed owner text, then invokes the existing controller with the current approval stage; no API, DTO, persistence, workflow, or server change is introduced.

Feedback history renders the serialized category and free text when the issue returns to Plan, blank feedback cannot submit, and an evidence loading or failure state does not create a new client-side approval authorization gate.

Focused pure, query, artifact-renderer, decision-surface, MobileActionBar, FeedbackHistory, and MSW-backed issue-detail tests cover Plan and Check success/failure matrices, exact action uniqueness, complete descriptor partitioning, Ask Agent and transcript secondary actions, disabled/pending secondary semantics, no-secondary omission, serialization, current-run scoping, responsive state sharing, and non-approval regression without real network or wall-clock time.

Focused Playwright scenarios against the production Web build cover both phone-width Plan and phone-width Check packages using controlled API responses: Plan shows proposal.md and long-token tasks.json, Check shows review.md and the diff summary, both avoid horizontal document overflow and safe-area overlap, both expose direct Approve and Send back controls without the generic action launcher, drawer, or dialog, and the optional More actions control does not cover or gate either direct action.

The phone Playwright workflows execute direct Approve and assert one approval request, then independently tap direct Send back once, verify the inline structured form opens and receives focus, choose a category, submit free text, and assert one correctly serialized feedback request; desktop inline evidence remains covered as a regression.

A phone approval Playwright fixture with Ask Agent and a concrete workflow session opens More actions and verifies both secondary entries are reachable; independent navigation assertions prove Ask Agent opens its composer route and View transcript opens the selected concrete session while Approve and Send back remain directly visible.

npm run typecheck -w packages/web, npm run test:run -w packages/web, and npm run test:browser -w packages/web -- tests/browser/issue-decision-surface.spec.ts pass with no Git-visible generated changes.
tasks.output: ApprovalReviewPackage with current-run Plan/Check evidence, reusable artifact and diff presentation, direct drawer-free mobile approval controls, complete secondary-action access, one responsive structured send-back form, issue-detail integration, and focused unit/spec/browser coverage.
tasks.notes: Keep this as one vertical slice because the package owns both responsive evidence and send-back draft state. Preserve the issue-453 ordered IssueDecisionAction descriptors and IssueDecisionActionController as the only action/dispatch sources; do not create an approval-only action model, revive InlineApprovalControls, parse tasks.json into a new model, block approval on evidence failure, or change Server contracts. Approval mode must not reuse MobileActionBar's generic action sheet or ConfirmationDrawer; only secondary descriptors use the compact non-modal menu, while non-approval states retain the generic mobile behavior unchanged. Unknown custom approval stages retain authorized actions and show an explicit no-configured-evidence state.

tasks.title: Add issue-detail keyboard actions
tasks.description: Add contextual desktop approval shortcuts to the completed review package and Command+Enter submission to its send-back form and the issue comment composer. Route every keyboard path through the same visible-control callbacks, validation, authorization, and pending safeguards, and make applicable bindings discoverable beside their controls.
acceptanceCriteria: While a desktop approval package is active, an unmodified non-repeating a invokes the enabled Approve descriptor exactly once through the existing controller and m opens the enabled shared send-back form; unavailable, pending, non-approval, and narrow-viewport states dispatch neither shortcut.

The approval listener ignores input, textarea, select, role=textbox, and contenteditable targets as well as modified keys and key repeat, cleans up on unmount or viewport/state change, and prevents default browser behavior only when it handles a shortcut.

Command+Enter in the shared send-back textarea invokes the same submit callback as its button exactly once when category/body validation passes and no request is pending; invalid, composing, repeating, or pending events do not dispatch again and plain Enter remains multiline input.

IssueCommentsSection centralizes button and keyboard submission behind one callback; Command+Enter forwarded by AttachmentComposer submits one nonblank non-pending comment exactly once, while blank, pending, composing, and repeating events do not submit and plain Enter remains multiline input.

Desktop approval controls visibly advertise a for Approve and m for Send back only when the matching action is available, and the displayed send-back and comment forms visibly advertise Command+Enter; the contextual bindings are not added to the application-wide shortcut catalogue.

Focused hook/component and MSW-backed issue-detail tests cover a/m success, editable-target suppression, modifier/repeat/pending/unavailable guards, cleanup, send-back and comment Command+Enter, plain Enter, invalid submissions, one request per keypress, and hint visibility.

The focused Playwright issue-decision-surface spec verifies desktop a approval, m form opening, visible shortcut hints, editable-field safety, Command+Enter send-back submission, and unchanged visible-control behavior against controlled API responses.

npm run typecheck -w packages/web, npm run test:run -w packages/web, and npm run test:browser -w packages/web -- tests/browser/issue-decision-surface.spec.ts pass with no Git-visible generated changes.
tasks.output: Contextual approval shortcut hook, guarded Command+Enter submission for send-back and comments, local shortcut hints, and focused unit/spec/browser coverage.
tasks.notes: Consumes T-001's ApprovalReviewPackage and controlled SendBackFeedbackForm. Keep single-key bindings page-local and desktop-only; do not introduce a global shortcut bus, change button semantics, add Ctrl+Enter beyond the specified Command+Enter contract, or bypass the shared action controller and form callbacks. The dependency graph is T-001 -> T-002 and is acyclic.
